definition: A private browsing feature that prevents your browser from storing local browsing history, cookies, and form data during your session.
metaDescription: Learn about incognito mode, its privacy benefits and limitations. Understand what it protects and what it doesn't when browsing privately.
simpleExplanation: Incognito mode is like using a temporary, disposable browser session. When you close the window, your browser forgets everything you did - no history, saved passwords, or cookies remain on your device.
whyItMatters: While incognito mode provides basic local privacy by not storing browsing data on your device, it doesn't make you invisible online. Websites, ISPs, and network administrators can still track your activity.
technicalDetail: Incognito mode creates an isolated browsing session that doesn't access existing cookies or save new ones permanently. However, it doesn't prevent IP address tracking, DNS queries, or fingerprinting techniques that websites use to identify visitors.

examples.explanation: Using incognito mode prevents gift searches from appearing in your browser history or influencing targeted ads that your family might see on shared devices.
Opening an incognito window at a library ensures your login sessions and browsing history aren't saved on the public computer after you leave.
Some news websites count article views using cookies, so incognito mode might reset this counter, though many sites now use more sophisticated tracking methods.

niche: Basic privacy protection for local browsing sessions
